lines.line: Summary: The Kremling Krew's foot soldiers. In Donkey Kong 64 they are simply called Kremlings, and they wear a sleeveless leather jacket with a skull-and-crossbones on the back.

quoted: Kritters (known as Kremlings in Donkey Kong 64 and DK: King of Swing) are enemies introduced in Donkey Kong Country. These Kremlings act as the main footsoldiers of the Kremling Krew
Kritters wear a sleeveless leather jacket with a skull-and-crossbones on the back

lines.line: Weak points: They are often the weakest Kremlings despite their muscular appearance, and the Prima guide says one hit will send them on their way.

quoted: They are often the weakest Kremlings despite their muscular appearance.
Prima Official Game Guide: Don't fear these reptilian nuisances. One hit will send them on their way.

lines.line: Tips: You meet them on Crocodile Isle and in every world except Fungi Forest and Creepy Castle. In Frantic Factory a red kind belches in a set order, and Lanky has to memorize it and repeat it to earn a Golden Banana.

quoted: They are encountered at Crocodile Isle, all worlds barring Fungi Forest and Creepy Castle
There is a red variety encountered in Frantic Factory, where they belch in a certain order for Lanky to memorize and replicate for a Golden Bananas

lines.line: Summary: A pink Kremling in a yellow-orange vest that throws unripe green oranges at the active Kong and can bounce a Kong backward with its belly.

quoted: They are now pink and wear a yellow-orange vest over their belly
Klumps attack the active Kong by throwing unripe, green oranges at them
Klumps can also bounce the Kong backward with their belly.

lines.line: Weak points: Klumps resist basic attacks, and a direct hit only stuns one for a while. They are truly beaten only by the shockwave attack, a thrown orange, an instrument move, or Chunky touching them in his Hunky Chunky state.

quoted: Klumps are among the stronger enemies, as they are resistant to basic attacks
the direct attack will only stun the Klump for a while
Klumps can only truly be defeated by the shockwave attack, throwing an orange, using a musical instrument, or if Chunky touches them while in his Hunky Chunky state.

lines.line: Tips: A beaten Klump salutes, falls over and leaves three oranges. You find them in every level except Frantic Factory, Creepy Castle and the DK Isles hub, and in Fungi Forest only by day, because Skeleton Kremlings take their place at night.

quoted: Klumps release three oranges upon defeat.
When defeated, Klump spins around, does a military salute and then falls down.
Klumps are encountered in every level except for Frantic Factory, Creepy Castle, and the DK Isles hub.
In Fungi Forest, Klumps only appear during the day time and are replaced by Skeleton Kremlings at night.

lines.line: Summary: A big, muscular Kremling in a leather jacket and sunglasses that guards a blueprint. It slams the ground to send out a shockwave and can punch a Kong that comes close.

quoted: They are large, muscular Kremlings
All Kasplats wear a leather jacket, sunglasses
Kasplats attack by slamming on the ground, unleashing a shockwave in the process. They can also punch the active Kong if they approach them.
They are King K. Rool's bodyguards, of whom he entrusted to guard the blueprints from Snide and the Kongs.

lines.line: Weak points: Kasplats are tough and often take several hits, but a Kong's shockwave attack or instrument move beats one in a single hit, and so do five oranges. Chunky can flatten one in Hunky Chunky mode, but then it drops no blueprint.

quoted: Kasplats are quite resilient, often requiring players to deliver multiple hits to defeat them.
the Kongs can defeat a Kasplat in a single hit by using their shockwave attack or musical instrument move. Alternatively, five oranges can defeat one.
this does not occur if Chunky Kong flattens a Kasplat while in Hunky Chunky mode

lines.line: Tips: Its hair colour shows which Kong can take its blueprint (yellow Donkey, red Diddy, blue Lanky, purple Tiny, green Chunky), and the hair turns white once the blueprint is taken. Every level has five Kasplats except Hideout Helm, which has none.

quoted: Kasplats have one of five hair colors: yellow, red, blue, purple or green, corresponding respectively to Donkey, Diddy, Lanky, Tiny or Chunky Kong.
Once a Kasplat's blueprint has been collected, the Kasplat's hair turns white.
Every level has five Kasplats, except for Hideout Helm, which does not feature any Kasplats

lines.line: Summary: A yellow flying enemy. Some Zingers dive-bomb the Kong on sight, and others drop unripe green oranges when they notice you.

quoted: Unlike previous games, Zingers are only seen in yellow.
They dive-bomb at the active Kong on sight in DK Isles and some of the earlier levels, while other Zingers drop unripe green Oranges upon noticing them.

lines.line: Weak points: An orange, an instrument move or a projectile shot defeats a Zinger. The ones that drop oranges generally respawn after you beat them, and the dive-bombers do not.

quoted: A Zinger can be defeated by an orange, a musical instrument move, or being shot by a projectile.
Unlike the dive-bombing Zingers, the orange-dropping ones will generally respawn after defeating them.

lines.line: Tips: They appear on DK Isles and in Jungle Japes, Angry Aztec, Gloomy Galleon, Crystal Caves and, by day only, Fungi Forest, where bats replace them at night. Frantic Factory has robotic Mechanical Zingers instead, and in Angry Aztec a beaten Zinger that falls into the sand burns up and leaves no melon slice.

quoted: Zingers also appear in Jungle Japes, Angry Aztec, Gloomy Galleon (where one is inside of a mechanical fish), Fungi Forest during the daytime (Bats replace them at night), and Crystal Caves.
Zingers have a robotic variety named Mechanical Zingers, which appear in Frantic Factory in place of Zingers.
If a Zinger falls into the sand in Angry Aztec from being defeated, it disappears in a burst of flames without releasing any watermelon slice.

lines.line: Summary: The boss of Frantic Factory and the third boss of the game, a giant metallic jack-in-the-box. Tiny Kong fights him on a floor of 16 glowing tiles.

quoted: He is the boss of Frantic Factory and the third boss of the game
is a large jack-in-the-box from Donkey Kong 64.
Mad Jack is a giant metallic jack-in-the-box
Tiny Kong finds herself in a dark room with 16 glowing floor tiles

lines.line: Weak points: Pound the switch on the tile that matches the tile Mad Jack stands on with a Simian Slam to electrocute him, and five hits end the fight. The other switch shocks Tiny instead and costs her half a Watermelon of health.

quoted: Tiny must attack Mad Jack by using Simian Slam on the switch on the same-colored tile as Mad Jack's. This causes the tile to electrocute Mad Jack.
by hitting the other switch, Tiny Kong is electrocuted instead, causing her to lose half of a Watermelon in health.
After being electrocuted a fifth time, the floor tile that Mad Jack is standing on collapses.

lines.line: Tips: While he hops, glide between tiles with Pony Tail Twirl, since he cannot hop diagonally. After the fourth hit he turns invisible, so follow the sparkles he leaves as he jumps. Falling off the stage does not lose the fight: a tile on the lower floor lifts Tiny back.

quoted: Tiny must glide between the floor tiles by using Pony Tail Twirl to hop between platforms. Mad Jack cannot hop diagonally.
After taking a fourth hit, Mad Jack becomes invisible and hops around on the tiles 15 times. In order to track where Mad Jack is, Tiny must watch the sparkles that trail behind him as he jumps.
If Tiny accidentally falls off the stage, she does not lose at the boss battle. Instead, a floor tile from the lower floor can return Tiny back to fighting Mad Jack.

lines.line: Summary: The boss of Gloomy Galleon, a huge pufferfish. Lanky Kong fights it from a small coconut-half motorboat in a pool, after 250 bananas have been fed to Scoff to open the boss door.

quoted: Puftoss, also known as Blowfish Baddie, Sea Spike, or the Pufferfish, is a massive yellowish Puftup and the boss of Gloomy Galleon in Donkey Kong 64.
Fighting Puftoss requires that 250 bananas be fed to Scoff at the Troff 'n' Scoff location in order for Troff to unlock the door that leads to the battle against Puftoss.
Lanky Kong is the Kong who is selected to fight Puftoss.
sitting inside of a small motorboat shaped like a coconut half

lines.line: Weak points: Drive the boat through all five DK stars before each one's timer runs out to bring electric poles up from the water, which shock Puftoss. A fifth hit defeats him.

quoted: Lanky can damage Puftoss by bringing electrical poles out from the water by driving through all five DK stars, each having a 30-second timer and resetting as he drives through each one. If done on time, the poles generate an electric current that electrocutes Puftoss, otherwise the poles go back into the water.
Puftoss is defeated after a fifth hit

lines.line: Tips: The star timers start at 30 seconds and shrink to 25, 20, 15 and finally 10 in later rounds. Puftoss cannot hurt Lanky by touching him, but he spits fireballs, and in round two his water slams make shockwaves that vanish when they touch an electric pole.

quoted: each having a 30-second timer
The DK stars become increasingly smaller in round, and their corresponding timer decreases by five seconds: starting with 25, then 20, followed by 15, and lastly 10 seconds.
Puftoss cannot damage Lanky on contact.
In the second round, he shoots out four fireballs and slams the water, creating two blue shockwaves, which disappear on contact with the electric poles.

lines.line: Summary: The boss of Creepy Castle and the seventh, next-to-last boss of the game: a crude cardboard cut-out of King K. Rool worked by two Kritters, fought in an arena walled by a castle rampart, in the rain.

quoted: King Kut Out, also known as Cardboard K. Rool, Kardboard K.Rool, and K. Rool Cut-Out, is a giant, crude cardboard cut-out of King K. Rool created and operated by two Kritters.
It is the boss of Creepy Castle and serves as the seventh and penultimate boss of Donkey Kong 64.
The battle arena takes place outside during a rainstorm.
The location itself is enclosed by a castle rampart in the shape of a square.

lines.line: Weak points: Step into the Barrel Cannon that faces it and blast into it. The ninth hit destroys it and the Boss Key drops in the middle of the arena.

quoted: To attack King Kut Out, the active Kong must enter the cannon facing King Kut Out and blast into it.
After another three hits, more specifically the ninth hit, King Kut Out is destroyed and its head falls off.
The Boss Key appears in the center of the arena for the Kongs to obtain.

lines.line: Tips: A shot with bad timing blasts the Kong out of the arena for good, and the next Kong comes out of the Tag Barrel (by default Tiny, then Chunky, Donkey and Diddy after Lanky). After the third hit a darker decoy follows it from the opposite wall, and blasting at the decoy throws you out. After three more hits it moves faster, so fire just as it appears in front of you; the ghosts that spawn near the cannons can be beaten to regain health.

quoted: if their timing is off, the active Kong blasts out of the arena and cannot re-enter.
The next Kong appears from the Tag Barrel, fought in a default order of: Tiny Kong, Chunky Kong, Donkey Kong, and lastly Diddy Kong.
Lanky Kong is the one specifically chosen by the boss door to fight King Kut Out.
After hitting King Kut Out a third time, its right arm breaks off. After this, a decoy of King Kut Out follows it around, always appearing from the opposite wall.
The Kong must not blast at the duplicate, or otherwise are blasted directly out of the arena.
After being hit three more times, King Kut Out's left arm breaks off and it moves even faster
To hit King Kut Out, the active Kong must immediately blast from the cannon just when King Kut Out appears from the wall in front.
they can also be defeated to regain health.

lines.line: Summary: Donkey Kong's own supply of bananas from his hoard, which the Kremlings steal and the Kongs have to recover. There are 200 in the seven worlds and DK Isles, plus a hidden 201st.

quoted: Golden Bananas, or Gold Bananas, are Donkey Kong's supply of bananas that he keeps in his banana hoard.
King K. Rool orders the Kremlings to steal the Golden Bananas
the Golden Bananas also have to be recovered by his four sidekicks
There are a total of 200 Golden Bananas to collect in the seven worlds and the hub location, DK Isles.
There is a hidden 201st Golden Banana that Tiny can obtain from the Banana Fairy Princess, once every Banana Fairy is caught.

lines.line: Uses: B. Locker keeps you out of the other worlds until you carry a minimum number of Golden Bananas, a different number for each world. Snide also pays one for every blueprint you bring him.

quoted: B. Locker allows them to enter if they have at least a minimum of a certain number of Golden Bananas (the requirement is different for each world).
Snide rewards them with a Golden Banana for every one they return.

lines.line: Tips: Each Kong has to collect five in every world by finishing their own tasks, 25 per world in all. The hidden 201st is larger and carries the Rare logo, and all 201 are needed for 101 percent and the second ending.

quoted: the Kongs each have to collect five Golden Bananas in every world by fulfilling their own unique tasks and challenges, for a total of 25 Golden Bananas per world.
which is larger in size and sports the Rare logo
All 201 Golden Bananas are required for achieving a 101% completion rating and unlocking the second ending.

lines.line: Summary: The design plans for the Blast-o-Matic, which the Kongs recover for Snide. There are 40 in all, five in every area except Hideout Helm, one for each Kong.

quoted: Blueprints in Donkey Kong 64 are the design plans for the Blast-o-Matic. They are collectible items that the Kongs must recover for Snide. There are 40 blueprints in total.
Aside from Hideout Helm, every area in the game, including DK Isles, has five blueprints, one for each Kong to collect.

lines.line: Uses: Each Kong takes their blueprints to Snide's H.Q. and gets a Golden Banana for every one. In Hideout Helm each blueprint also delays the Blast-o-Matic's countdown by a minute.

quoted: Each Kong can individually visit Snide's H.Q. with their recovered blueprints, where Snide rewards them with a Golden Banana for every one they return.
Snide uses the blueprints to delay the Blast-o-Matic's countdown timer by a minute per blueprint.

lines.line: Tips: Every blueprint is guarded by a Kasplat whose hair colour matches the Kong who can take it, and the wrong Kong sees only a hologram. The Helm countdown starts at ten minutes and can reach 50 with all 40, and once you have recovered them all Snide lets you replay most of the bonus stages.

quoted: Every blueprint is guarded by a Kasplat, whose hair color and blueprint color corresponds to a specific Kong
If an incorrect Kong is active, the blueprint appears in the form of a hologram, and the Kong cannot collect it.
By default, the timer starts at ten minutes and can count down from 50 minutes at highest, if all 40 blueprints were collected beforehand.
after the Kongs recover every blueprint, Snide allows the Kongs to replay most of the Bonus Stages from a sub-menu at his headquarters.

lines.line: Summary: A collectable that fuels each Kong's barrel ability. They are fairly common in most levels, especially where an ability is needed.

quoted: Crystal Coconuts are used as fuel for each Kong's Kong Barrel ability
They are semi-common items that appear in most levels, especially in areas requiring the Kongs to use their ability.

lines.line: Uses: The coconuts become active once a Kong learns their ability at Cranky's Lab. Strong Kong makes Donkey Kong invincible and lets him cross quicksand and lava, but it ends when the coconuts run out or he uses a Bananaport Pad, and Lanky's OrangSprint burns more coconuts the longer he runs.

quoted: When a Kong learns their ability from Cranky's Lab, the Crystal Coconuts become activated.
Donkey Kong cannot be damaged in his Strong Kong form, also allowing him to move across surfaces such as quicksand and lava.
Strong Kong is powered by Crystal Coconuts, so if Donkey Kong runs out of Crystal Coconuts, the ability wears off.
Donkey Kong also loses the power if he uses a Bananaport Pad.
The longer Lanky performs the OrangSprint, the more Crystal Coconuts he will use up.

lines.line: Tips: A Kong starts able to carry 20, and each Banana Fairy you catch adds one, up to 40 with all 20 fairies. Catching every fairy also unlocks a cheat in the Mystery menu for unlimited coconuts.

quoted: At first, the Kongs can only carry up to 20 Crystal Coconuts, though for each Banana Fairy captured, one more gets added to their maximum. By capturing all 20 Banana Fairies, the Kongs can carry up to 40 Crystal Coconuts
Capturing every Banana Fairy unlocks a cheat from the Mystery menu that allows for infinite Crystal Coconuts to be used

lines.line: Summary: A brown medal with a banana in the middle, earned by collecting 75 bananas of your own colour in a level.

quoted: They are brown medals with a banana spinning in their centers.
A Kong can obtain a Banana Medal by collecting 75 bananas of their corresponding color in a level.

lines.line: Uses: There are 40 in all, eight for each Kong, and having 15 lets you play Jetpac in Cranky's Lab. Every medal is needed for 101 percent.

quoted: There is a total of 40 Banana Medals, with eight for each Kong to obtain.
If the Kongs have at least 15 Banana Medals, the Kongs can play a classic Rareware title from Cranky's Lab, Jetpac.
Every Banana Medal is required for 101% completion.

lines.line: Tips: In Hideout Helm a Kong earns a medal by finishing two Bonus Barrel challenges instead. The five medals there are lost for good if you leave their rooms without collecting them, which ends any chance of 101 percent.

quoted: In the final level, Hideout Helm, the criterion for obtaining a Banana Medal is different, as each Kong can obtain one after completing two Bonus Barrel challenges.
The five that appear, however, become permanently unobtainable if the Kongs leave the rooms without collecting them, preventing the player from achieving 101% completion.

lines.line: Summary: Each Kong buys a personal weapon from Funky Kong for three Banana Bunch Coins: the Coconut Shooter for Donkey, Peanut Popguns for Diddy, the Grape Shooter for Lanky, the Feather Bow for Tiny and the Pineapple Launcher for Chunky.

quoted: Funky sells a weapon to the active Kong if they pay three Banana Bunch Coins:
Donkey Kong: Coconut Shooter
Diddy Kong: Peanut Popguns
Lanky Kong: Grape Shooter
Tiny Kong: Feather Bow
Chunky Kong: Pineapple Launcher

lines.line: Uses: A weapon has limited ammo. Donkey's Coconut Shooter shoots Banana Balloons, hits Coconut Switches and snipes enemies from afar, and a Supply Crate gives it five coconuts. Funky's Store, in every level except Hideout Helm, refills any Kong's ammo.

quoted: The Coconut Shooter has a limited supply of coconut ammo, which Donkey Kong can use to shoot Banana Balloons, hit Coconut Switches, and snipe enemies from afar.
Supply Crates (each providing five coconuts)
The Kongs can also visit Funky's Store to have their ammo supply replenished if it is below the maximum amount.
Funky's Store appears in every level except Hideout Helm.

lines.line: Tips: Every weapon holds up to 50 ammo at first. Ammo Belt 1 (3 coins, from Frantic Factory) raises that to 100, Homing Ammo (5, from Fungi Forest) makes shots home in on enemies, Ammo Belt 2 (5, from Crystal Caves) raises it to 200, and the Sniper Scope (7, from Creepy Castle) lets shots go farther in first-person view.

quoted: By default, every Kong's weapon only carries up to 50 ammo.
Ammo Belt 1 || 3 Banana Bunch Coins || Increases the maximum capacity of the Kongs' weapons to 100 ammo, and increases their orange capacity from 20 to 25. || Frantic Factory
Homing Ammo || 5 Banana Bunch Coins || Allows the Kongs to use homing ammo, which causes their shots to home in on enemies.
|| Fungi Forest || Ammo Belt 2 || 5 Banana Bunch Coins || Increases the maximum capacity of the Kongs' weapons to 200 ammo, and their orange capacity to 30. || Crystal Caves
Sniper Scope || 7 Banana Bunch Coins || Allows the Kongs to shoot ammo farther while in a first-person view. || Creepy Castle
